newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended up in dull trading on Wednesday on short-covering following sharp falls over the past few days, traders said.
The only traded October contract ended at 1,900 yuan ($228) per tonne, rising 15 yuan. It opened at 1,900 and stayed at that level for the whole session.
Combined volume fell to 600 tonnes from 1,200.
Traders said technical overselling was responsible for today's rises but the future trend of rice futures was still unclear.
"Falls during the past few days triggered some short-covering but few investors wanted to buy due to an uncertain market trend," one trader said.
"Institutions controlled the market and no one knows what they will do tommorrow," he added.
Some traders expect rice to fall in the next few days with few investors wanting to buy at the current level.
